research_findings: The system handles feature requests through Next.js server actions. The waitlist signup action was missing rate limiting, making it vulnerable to abuse.
The application uses Next.js app router and has access to headers for IP-based rate limiting.
A simple sliding-window rate limiter using in-memory Map is sufficient for protecting low-traffic endpoints before needing Redis.
features_improved: Secured the waitlist signup endpoint against abuse by adding an IP-based rate limiter.
new_features_added: Introduced a generic `rateLimit` utility in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` using an in-memory sliding window, which can be reused across other server actions.
next_steps_for_next_run: Migrate the in-memory rate limiter to a distributed store (e.g., Redis via @upstash/ratelimit) to ensure consistency across multiple serverless instances.
Apply the new rate limiter to other sensitive server actions like password resets or form submissions.
